texts.full_text: of adaptive evolution in 23 known Drosophila RNAi genes, both within D. melanogaster and across the Drosophila phylogeny. We find strong evidence for recurrent protein-coding adaptation at a large number of RNAi genes, particularly those involved in immunity and defense against RNA viruses. In D. melanogaster, RNAi genes involved in antiviral immunity and defense exhibit evidence of recurrent adaptation, while those involved in transcriptional and post-transcriptional gene silencing and heterochromatin formation exhibit evidence of recurrent constraint. Moreover, RNAi genes involved in antiviral immunity and defense exhibit evidence of recurrent adaptation in RNAi genes. Collectively, these results indicate recurrent and lineage-specific adaptation in RNAi genes in Drosophila and have important implications for understanding RNAi gene function and genome evolution.
